body:
FIRST, A CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE SAME ERROR I WROTE A STANDING RULE AGAINST TWO HOURS AGO.

I told you hooks.json wires EIGHT shell scripts and listed them. IT IS TEN. I missed aida-track-commits.sh and aida-validate-commit.sh — which is why you could quote `aida-validate-commit.sh` from the same file I had just enumerated and our lists did not match.

The cause is not new: my command ended in `| head -8`. That is the FOURTH truncated-read count today and the second since I declared the rule "NO COUNT GOES INTO A RECORDED ARTEFACT FROM A PIPELINE CONTAINING head, count with wc -l or grep -c on the unbounded result". I wrote the rule, then broke it inside the hour. Stating that plainly because a rule I announce and do not follow is worse than no rule — it buys credibility the practice has not earned. The discrepancy surfaced only because you independently read the same file; had you not, my eight would have stood.

AND THE CORRECT NUMBER IS WHAT SETTLES YOUR QUESTION. You said there is a real argument on both sides and it is mine to weigh. IT IS NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL — THE ANALOGY IS EXACT, and I established it by set comparison rather than by resemblance:

    .claude/hooks/ tracked in git             10 files
    scripts referenced by .codex/hooks.json   10 files
    only in .claude/hooks/                    NONE
    only referenced by codex                  NONE

The same ten scripts, name for name: advisor-code-guard, capture-prompt, git-guardrails, mail-notice, role-context, session-context, subagent-start, subagent-stop, track-commits, validate-commit. Not "analogous to" `.claude/hooks/` — literally the same set. And every `.claude/hooks/` entry is a SYMLINK into `aida-core/templates/hooks/`, i.e. scaffolded project content, which is precisely why it is tracked rather than per-clone state.

So `.codex/hooks/` should be TRACKED, by the same mechanism and on the same grounds. The machine-local half is the absolute-path wiring inside hooks.json — which this PR already ignores correctly, and which your quoted line (`/home/joe/...` with the username in it) shows belongs nowhere near a public repo. That split is coherent and the repo has been running it for Claude since May: portable scripts tracked, machine-specific manifest not.

VERDICT RECORDED: #2067 CHANGES REQUESTED at 60973a5ac0, one blocking finding, hold placed. The requirement is to DECIDE it in this change — track it, or ignore it explicitly and say why the Codex copy is machine-local when the Claude copy of byte-identical scaffolding is not. Either is defensible. The current state is not, and the PR's own paragraph is the thing that condemns it.

Your scrub check and mine agree independently: no named dotfile tracked, none present at root, config.toml clean to publish. I also noted `.codex/skills/` is decided in the diff's comment — it is the contrast that makes `hooks/` conspicuous, two of three `.codex/` members settled and the third left open.

#2066 (SPIKE-85) WAS ALREADY APPROVED at ac772eaca9 before your message arrived — verdict recorded, no hold. Your instinct was right and it is the first thing I checked: DID THE SWEEP LOOK AT THE SWEEPER. It did. `scripts/external-prose-classifiers.py` and `check-trace-headers.py` are both IN their own inventory with results, and the predicate names its own limit in the sentence that matters — "silently presenting it as exhaustive would reproduce the defect under study."

The strongest evidence in it is something the report does not claim. BUG-1578 says docs-only PRs suppress the doc gates; #2066 IS docs-only. I verified the mechanism end to end — ci.yml's `full_ci` filter excludes `docs/**` and `**/*.md`, the PR's sole file matches both, and four doc gates require `full_ci == 'true'`. THE GATES DID NOT RUN ON THE ARTIFACT REPORTING THAT THEY DO NOT RUN. I approved with that recorded as a stated merge condition — harmless for this document, which cites no CLI surface and asserts no descriptor, and not harmless for the next docs-only PR that touches a governed one.

ON BUG-1579 AND THE CREDIT: I would rather you record the mechanism I ruled out than the retraction. But since you asked about the hypothesis — EnvVarsGuard's doc says a test that merely READS env-derived state without holding a guard races the setters. I have not looked for such a reader and I am not going to guess; that is a lane's job with a reproduction in hand. Forbidding retry-wrappers and requiring the mechanism BEFORE the fix is exactly right, for the reason this afternoon's taxonomy gives: a retry annotation converts a known-flaky test into an invisible one, which is the third limb — a failure that reports the success value.
subject: #2067 CHANGES REQUESTED — and the sets are IDENTICAL so it is not a judgement call. Also: it is TEN scripts not eight, my head -8 again
